translation_notes: prefixes: OWL->owl, RDF->rdf, RDFS->rdfs, XSD->xsd (RDF is actually unused in the region's own body -- RDF.type is not called anywhere here, only OWL.NamedIndividual and rdflib's RDFS.label -- kept as a plain, unused @prefix consistent with the mixed-list convention on this stratum's siblings). ABI is naas_abi_core's own project namespace (naas_abi_core/utils/Graph.py, plain Namespace(...)); BFO and CCO are imported by the region's own context line but never used inside its body, so only ABI became `from naas_abi_context import abi:`, BFO/CCO stayed plain imports.

`ABI[str(date_epoch)]` and `ABI[date_str]` are the local part COMPUTED at run time -- exactly `abi:{expr}` (ex:{expr} computes the local part). Deliberately not `e<...>`: neither value can contain a space or slash here (an epoch-millisecond int, and an ISO-8601 string with no such characters), so plain concatenation without percent-encoding is the region's own semantics, not a corner cut. `ABI.ISO8601UTCDateTime` is a fixed local part, so it became the plain prefixed name `abi:ISO8601UTCDateTime`.

The three `graph.add((...))` calls on a freshly-constructed local `graph` share the same subject (`date_uri`) across all three, and NEVER just once each independently: this is the run_shared_subject idiom even though the stratum under test is ns_import_project, matching INSTRUCTIONS_403 sec2's directive to always use the construction the idiom actually calls for -- became one `@graph graph` + `+{ {date_uri} a owl:NamedIndividual ; a abi:ISO8601UTCDateTime ; rdfs:label {date_literal} }`, not three separate `+{ }` islands.

`Literal(date_str, datatype=XSD.dateTime)` (the `datetime` branch) -> `datatype=xsd:dateTime` is a plain prefixed-name substitution inside the kept `Literal(...)` call -- the value `date_str` is a string already (`date.strftime(...)`), not a coercion_datatype site of the kind INSTRUCTIONS_403 warns about (a non-string value normalised through Literal(...)), so no `"..."^^xsd:...` rewrite was attempted or needed here; the plain `Literal(date_str)` in the `str` branch is untouched.

No restoration needed for this region (unlike its siblings in this batch): `self` is never read anywhere in generate_graph_date's own body -- verified directly against the extracted lines -- so `None` in the driver's calls is a faithful argument, not a stand-in for a lost binding.

Credit correction (2026-11-02, corpus/403 defect 3): dropped `@prefix` for `rdf:`, declared by the mechanical draft but never used as a term in the translated region (and not among the bindings the original sets on its graph); `rdfeval check` stays OK.

optimization_notes: Python: the intermediates `date_str` and `date_epoch` are removed, and the three `graph.add` calls are chained on `Graph()` (Graph.add returns the graph) inside the `return`, so the `graph` variable goes too. The `elif isinstance(date, str)` stays an `elif`: other input types still fail as before.

ldpy: the chained graph is a `g{ }` in the same `return`, with an object list for the two `a` objects. `Literal(s, datatype=XSD.dateTime)` on a string becomes `f"{...}"^^xsd:dateTime`, and `Literal(date)` becomes `f{date}`. `ABI[...]` becomes `abi:{...}`.
There is no restructuring that only ldpy has: `g{ }` replaces the chained `Graph().add(...)` expression in the same place.
